verdict.rationale: three.js ships numbered releases (npm reports 0.186.0), and its official Migration Guide wiki has per-release sections (e.g. 185→186) linked from the release notes, so versioned APIs and documented breaking changes are evidenced. However, the pack shows no formal deprecation policy: no stated deprecation windows, no semver stability guarantees (it stays on 0.x), and llms.txt simply tells users to always use the latest version. Missing for 10: an explicit documented deprecation policy with timelines, stable or semver-guaranteed API versioning, and independent corroboration of upgrade stability.
